analysis.headline: LPG under-recovery projected to reach ₹370 per cylinder by December
analysis.hook: State refiners face growing losses on cooking gas supplied to 33 crore households.
gist: Indian Oil Corporation projects LPG losses reaching ₹370 per cylinder by December 2026.
Unrecovered costs squeeze profitability for public sector oil marketing companies.
Government fiscal support or potential retail price adjustments in coming quarters.
analysis.what_happened: Indian Oil Corporation (IOC) projects under-recoveries on Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) will rise to ₹309 per cylinder in November 2026 and ₹370 per cylinder in December 2026. IOC reported volatile crude procurement costs in the second quarter, fluctuating between discounts and premiums. Cooking fuel sold at below-market rates impacts supply to over 33 crore households across India.

who_is_affected.effect: Financial margins face compression as unabsorbed fuel costs accumulate on balance sheets.
Retail prices remain suppressed for now, though potential future policy changes could alter end-user costs.

sectors.why: Selling domestic cooking gas below procurement cost increases financial under-recoveries for state refiners.

chain: Volatile global crude and procurement costs increase raw material expenses for LPG.
Retail prices for cooking gas are kept below market rates to protect consumers.
Oil marketing companies absorb the shortfall, generating under-recoveries.
Accumulating shortfalls compress operating margins and cash flows of state refiners.
transmission_mechanism.explanation: High volatile crude procurement costs drive up the landed cost of LPG for domestic oil companies. Because domestic cooking gas is sold at regulated price points below market parity, refiners cannot immediately pass increased costs onto consumers. Over a horizon of weeks to months, this shortfall manifests as under-recoveries on company balance sheets, reaching an estimated ₹370 per cylinder by December 2026. Ultimately, these unrecovered costs reduce quarterly profitability unless offset by government compensation.

analysis.market_reaction: No market reaction reported in these sources.

bull_case.argument: Market bulls argue that potential government subsidies or eventual crude price moderation will compensate state refiners for unabsorbed losses.
depends_on: Timely cash infusion or subsidy support from the central government
Stabilisation or decline in international crude oil procurement prices

bear_case.argument: Bears contend that prolonged uncompensated under-recoveries will erode working capital and weigh heavily on earnings for oil marketing firms.
depends_on: Sustained elevated global crude procurement costs
Delay or lack of government budget allocation to cover LPG under-recovery gaps

variables_to_watch.why_it_matters: Determines whether oil refiners receive direct fiscal compensation for LPG under-recoveries
Influences the extent of under-recovery gap per cylinder in November and December 2026

analysis.confidence_reason: Both news sources directly quote executive statements from Indian Oil Corporation regarding specific projected figures.

jargon.plain_meaning: The loss incurred by state-owned fuel retailers when selling products below their actual market-aligned cost.
